I’ll need to identify a source by finding a node with no incoming connections, possibly at the endpoint.**Determining graph components**

I'm trying to figure out if Kenneth and Kayla are in the same directed path. I'm looking to identify possible invalid steps in my analysis by checking if each adjacent pair appears in a statement, regardless of direction, and they do. This means they're connected. It seems both endpoints can be sinks if the middle node has an out-degree of 2. But I assumed a max out-degree of 1, which might not always hold true.**Analyzing graph paths**

I'm thinking about how paths work in directed graphs. For instance, if I have a component like A->B<-C, that has B with two incoming connections, which isn't allowed. A->B->C is fine because B has one incoming and one outgoing. So, I realize that the only valid orientations are when all arrows go the same way, or are all reversed. If I change directions, I create nodes with two incoming or outgoing connections, which disrupts the structure.
